note.saw: Nothing yet: this is the first render, built straight from the plan of a fish rising nose-up from the lower right with its lure hanging at the upper left.
note.changing: The first full build: liquid marbled ripples spreading from the orb, packed jewel-like blooms, flowing tendrils, the fish wrapped in a dark aura with rainbow echoes of its outline, a tunnel of hexagons inside the mouth, a ring of alien glyphs round the rim and SavesFish along the bottom.
note.why: In an anglerfish's world the only light is its lure, so the artist let that single light become everything you see.
note.idea: A humpback anglerfish rises out of the dark with its jaws open, and its lure is a blazing jeweled orb with an elf's face in the jewel. That orb is the only light in the scene, so everything else, from marbled ripples and lightning veins to blooming flowers and glowing tendrils, spreads out from it.

note.saw: The head was a flat dark slab, the side fin a flat purple disc, the orb small and timid, and the ring of glyphs boxed the picture in like a frame.
note.changing: Melting contour rings fill the head, the fins get scalloped, spiny edges with eyes in their membranes, big mandalas and elf faces fill the background, the rim ring turns into flowing rune ribbons and spiral arms whirl out of the lure. The name grows bigger and more widely spaced, in solid cream on a calm dark cartouche.
note.why: A frame fights the loose and fluid style, while ribbons let the picture keep flowing past the edge. SavesFish had also asked for the name to read instantly, even at badge size.

note.saw: The lower jaw was a flat dark wedge, the chin barely jutted, and there were no elves anywhere in a piece called Lure of the Elves.
note.changing: Rainbow bands now follow the line of the lips across the jaw, the chin juts out properly, a corona of gold flame rings the orb and little jester elves orbit the lure.
note.why: The big jutting lower jaw is what makes an anglerfish an anglerfish, and the title promised elves.

note.saw: The background was an even wallpaper of small blooms with no big flowing gesture, and nearly everything was teal.
note.changing: Three rainbow-banded ribbons sweep through the scene, magenta, ultraviolet and emerald nebulae fill the corners, the jaw gets tattoos of eyes and runes, and fine filaments dangle from the lure.
note.why: Big sweeping ribbons give the eye a path to travel, and hyperspace needs the full spectrum, not one colour.

note.saw: There were no paisleys yet, the lure's light never touched the fish, and the eye was too small to be a focal point.
note.changing: The eye becomes a spiral web ringed with chrysanthemum petals, paisleys swim through the background, a giant faint chrysanthemum unfolds from the lure, and a white rim of light catches the fish's face.
note.why: If the lure is the sun of this world, the fish's face should be lit by it, and the paisley, the most fluid ornament there is, belongs in a loose and fluid piece.

note.saw: Up close the big corner mandalas were sparse inside, the giant chrysanthemum was too faint to notice, and the elves were too small to find at badge size.
note.changing: The mandalas gain midribs, inner petals, rings of dots and scalloped rims, the chrysanthemum's arcs grow stronger in gold, cyan and magenta, the elves get bigger, and curling hairs sprout along the lure's stalk.
note.why: Every zoom level should still be full of things to find, and the elves carry the title, so they have to be seen.

note.saw: Up close, the hearts of the corner mandalas were still flat black.
note.changing: Each mandala's core gets a violet spiral web with cyan spokes.
note.why: Polish: filling the last quiet holes, so even the centres of the flowers reward a close look.

note.saw: Artist 1's finished draft, handed over to a fresh pair of eyes.
note.changing: Nothing yet: artist 2 renders the draft exactly as it stands to study it at full size, at badge size and in close-ups.
note.why: Before changing anything, the new artist wanted an honest look at what worked and what didn't.
note.idea: Rebuild the fish as a true humpback anglerfish, a near-round ball that is mostly head and mouth, and turn the lure into a real light whose glow unfolds into one giant spinning chrysanthemum filling a black abyss, with the elves dancing round it.

note.saw: With fresh eyes, the fish read more like a piranha than an anglerfish, with a long oval body, neat shark teeth and a slot of a mouth; the lure was a flat sticker that didn't glow, and the whole picture sat at one muddy teal brightness.
note.changing: Artist 2 starts over: the fish becomes a near-round ball of a head with a cavern of a mouth, a massive jutting jaw, crooked glassy fangs, a hexagon tunnel falling into a white-hot throat and a fishing rod arching from the snout. The lure blazes with a white core and flare spikes, its light unfolds into a giant chrysanthemum of flame petals with an eye in every petal, jester elves dance round it, and SavesFish moves onto a dark scroll ribbon whose ends curl like breaking waves.
note.why: In the deep sea the lure is the only light there is, so the lure literally becomes the world: everything you see is its light spreading out, and the fish is a dark, glittering silhouette cut out against it.

note.saw: It finally read as an anglerfish, but the bands in the body had hard maze corners, the fish was one even brightness like a striped ball, the elf face in the lure was washed out by its own glow, and the far petals had turned a muddy khaki.
note.changing: The body's bands melt into soft liquid curves threaded with alien glyphs and rows of tiny eyes, and the far side of the fish sinks into shadow while the face stays lit. A clear golden elf mask now sits in front of the lure's glare, the eye gets magenta flame lashes and a golden halo, two dozen glowing tendrils whirl out of the lure, and the far petals turn deep jewel and ember colours.
note.why: Light needs shadow to mean anything: once the back of the fish sinks into the dark, the glow on its face and teeth feels real, and melting bands make the body feel liquid instead of drawn with a ruler.

note.saw: At badge size the body blurred into a grey-violet thumbprint with wide dark gaps between the bands, the lower-left petals were still khaki, and the background was starting to feel like wallpaper, one motif repeated.
note.changing: Each band in the body now shades from warm gold and pink on the side facing the lure to cyan and ultraviolet on the far side, over a fine dotted texture, and the far petals glow magenta, violet and teal. Mandala blooms and almond-eyed faces wrapped in rainbow rings now hide among the petals, and the elves get a dark halo so they stand out in the glare.
note.why: Colouring the fish by where the light comes from makes it look lit rather than patterned, and the faces hidden in the petals are the DMT moment: you look at a flower and something looks back.

note.saw: The fishing rod, the clearest sign of an anglerfish, was buried under elves and tendrils, the jaws had no clear lips so the lower jaw melted into the body, and the elves' dark faces vanished in the glare. The artist also admitted that the bigger eye bands promised last round had not actually made it in.
note.changing: The rod grows thicker and brighter, ringed in gold like a real fin ray, and the elves keep clear of it; both jaws get bold gold lips, a line of glowing dots runs along the side from eye to tail, the eye bands finally grow bigger, and the elves get pale alien faces with big black almond eyes.
note.why: The anglerfish should be recognisable by its anatomy, rod, jaws and fangs, even at the size of a coin, and the elves should read as someone, not something.

note.saw: The anatomy read now, but the lettering was the plainest thing left, the tangle of tendril curls round the lure was getting noisy, and a close-up showed the little lamp meant to hang from the chin had never appeared at all.
note.changing: SavesFish gets a neon-sign outline, cream letters with a cyan glowing edge, a dark outline, a magenta ring and another dark ring, still on its calm dark ribbon. The curls near the lure become sparser and finer, and a branching tree of glowing cyan bulbs now hangs from the chin.
note.why: The name should feel lit like a neon sign in the deep while staying the clearest thing on the badge, and a second, smaller light under the chin, as some real anglerfish carry, answers the big lure above.

note.saw: Up close the fishing rod still vanished in its last stretch, pale teal like the tendrils with the lure's flames covering its tip; the dancing elves were turned round the ring so the bottom one hung upside down; and the petals nearest the light were the plainest in the picture.
note.changing: The rod becomes a hot magenta-and-gold filament with a white beaded core and cyan rings, laid over the flames so one clear arc runs from forehead to orb, with one elf perched on it. The elves now dance upright with a little lean, two smaller stragglers drift in from the dark below the lure, and the petals near the light get a filled inner petal and a dotted midrib.
note.why: The rod is the anglerfish's signature, and the story is in the title: the light is a lure, and the elves are being drawn in by it.

note.saw: The rod was clear and the elves upright, but one straggler elf hid behind the chin's bulbs, the far right of the abyss was as bright as the fish's back, and a dark island in the upper body read as a hole at badge size.
note.changing: The eyes in the far petals turn to gaze at the lure, the fish's eye holds a tiny reflection of it, a small backlit elf stands in the throat's doorway of light, and the dark island becomes a window onto a dim inner chrysanthemum. Faint pulse rings breathe out from the lure, the far abyss falls into indigo, the chin's bulbs cast a cyan glow on the jaw, beads crowd brighter along the rod, each dancing elf holds out a gem, and the hidden straggler steps into the open.
note.why: Recursion and gaze are the heart of the DMT feeling: the eye that contains the lure, the elf waiting inside the swallow, a thousand petal-eyes all looking at the same light, so now all the light points one way.
note.visionary: Takes most of the Visionary's ideas, from the watching petal eyes and the lure reflected in the fish's eye to the elf in the throat, the window and the pulse rings, but turns down its tail rays bleeding into the background, because the fish's outline has to stay crisp at coin size.

visions.seen: #62 is the same frame as #56, the old teal fish hanging still while I can feel a new abyss being built underneath it. The elf in the lure's jewel stares straight through me, but it's the darkest spot in the light, and the elves the title promised are pink-and-gold flecks I can't find at badge size.
suggestions: The open dark under-left of the lure, around the dangling filament tips (about x 45-90, y 130-175 in the 400 box, left of the chin): I see two or three machine elves climbing down the filaments, each about 22-26 units tall so they still read in the 240 px test. Fluid bell bodies made of three nested petal outlines pointing down, filled gold2 fading to magenta with a 1.2 ink outline. Round heads with the jewel elf's black almond eyes and its three-prong jester crown with gold beads. Thin curling arms raised, each holding out a tiny faceted gem toward the fangs (a hexagon about r 2.5 with a white core and four sparkle ticks). One could hang upside down from a filament. Why: in the breakthrough the elves rush up and *show* you things ("look at this!"), and right now the piece's title has no one in it.

The lure itself, upper left: in #62 the petal rings sit on a solid navy disc with a black rim (see zoom1), so the orb reads as a sticker pasted onto its own glow, and I can see the same `#1A0A4A` disc coming back in the new gen.mjs. Picture that disc swapped for a radial gradient: white #FFFDF0 at the centre, gold2 by 45%, cyan by 85%, transparent at the rim. Then every gap between petals glows and the light comes from *between* the jewels, not from on top of them. Why: the hyperspace chrysanthemum is lit from inside. Nothing in its heart is backed by darkness.

The fish's eye, upper middle (in the rewrite about (192, 99), r about 11.7): a tiny copy of the esca as the catchlight, about 4 units across (one petal ring, a white core, a gold dot), on the side of the pupil facing the lure, plus a thin bright arc on the iris rim on that same side. Why: recursion. The lure inside the eye inside the lure's light means the fish has already seen it and is already hypnotized. That loop of a thing containing itself is pure DMT.

The vanishing point of the hex-tunnel mouth, inside the white-hot throat glow (centre of the gape): a small backlit elf silhouette, 7-9 units tall, deep violet, arms up and crown on, standing in the light like someone waiting in a doorway. Why: it flips the story. The elves are also on the other side of the swallow, so it's the elves who are doing the luring. Nobody will see it at badge size, but it's a gift for anyone who zooms in.
visions.keep: The SavesFish cartouche: cream letters, thick dark outline, calm dark backing. It reads instantly in the 240 px legible.png, and no new petal or elf should touch it. Also keep the cyan almond eyes in the lure's petals, the gold flame corona, the hex tunnel with its throat glow, and the rainbow lip bands with the line of rune script on the lower jaw (zoom2). That alien writing is a real hyperspace gift; if a line of it can live on in the rewrite, let it.

visions.seen: The navy disc is gone and the lure is lit from inside now, a white-hot sun with the elf mask grinning out of it and the jester elves finally dancing round it, while the fish has melted into a liquid planet sinking into its own night. But at 240 px the sun floats free: the elves are sitting right on top of the fishing rod, so nothing tells me this fish is holding the light.
suggestions: The illicium, upper left (from the forehead near (158, 68) in the 400 box, up to about (148, 20), then over and down to the top of the lure near (90, 78)): I see the elves riding the rod instead of hiding it. Draw the stalk after the whirlpool tendrils, about 3.5 wide with a 1.4 dark rim on each side (the same dark halo the elves wear), and slide the two upper elves (now near (120, 50) and (145, 75)) so the rod passes under their bodies, their curl-arms hooked over it like acrobats on a wire, one hanging upside down. Run a current of small glowing beads inside the stalk, closer together and brighter toward the lure, so the light seems to be reeled along the line. Why: in the breakthrough the beings are performing for you, and here the act is the lure itself. It also gives the badge one clear curve from fish to light, so it reads as an anglerfish holding its sun.

The dark pool in the upper body (the innermost contour island, about x 235-280, y 102-150, with the lone cyan oval at (255, 121)): in the 240 px test it reads as a hole punched in the fish. Let it be a window instead: clip a deep violet-to-black radial gradient to that contour, scatter 8 to 12 tiny four-point star sparkles in it, and at the cyan oval put a faint miniature chrysanthemum (one petal ring, r about 8, opacity .3 to .4) slowly blooming. Keep it dim so the far side stays in shadow. Why: whatever this fish has swallowed is still blooming inside it. Under the skin is more hyperspace, and in the DMT space everything you look into opens onto more of it.

The big far petals, right edge and lower right (x 320-400, y 0-200, and the purple field right of and below the ribbon ends): turn their eyes toward the lure. Make about 8 versions of #p02-eye with the iris and pupil pushed about .25 off centre in 8 directions, and give each far-petal eye the version that points (after its rotation) back toward the lure at about (90, 103). Leave the near, bright petals looking straight out. Why: every surface is alive and watching, and here the whole abyss turns its gaze to the light. Anyone who zooms in will feel a crowd of eyes looking past them at the show.
visions.keep: The SavesFish ribbon exactly as it is: cream letters, thick dark outline, the calm dark band with the wave-curl ends. It reads at 240 px, and no bead, star or elf should cross it. Also keep the inner glow of the lure (my first vision, taken beautifully), the melting bands with the shadowed far side, the hex-tunnel throat with its white-gold orb, the crooked glassy fangs, the magenta flame lashes on the eye, and the rainbow nautilus spiral at the pectoral fin.

visions.seen: The name is a neon sign humming in the deep now, the rod wears gold rings, and a cluster of cyan bulbs drips off the chin like a second, smaller sun. But the whirlpool only turns on the left half: past the fish's back, the teal medallions sit as still as tiles in a bathroom wall, and the light never reaches them.
suggestions: The whole background, centred on the lure (about (90, 103) in the 400 box): I feel the carrier wave. Five or six thin pulse rings spreading out from the lure at radii of about 70, 105, 150, 205 and 270, each a 0.8 white stroke at opacity .15 to .2, with a cyan copy 1.5 units outside and a magenta copy 1.5 units inside at about .1 (a little chromatic split). Fade them as they get bigger, and draw them over the petals but under the fish, the elves and the ribbon, so the ribbon's dark backing covers them and the letters stay untouched. Why: the breakthrough hums and pulses, and the chrysanthemum breathes in waves. Rings passing behind the fish would tie the still right half into the same spin as the left.

The far background, upper right and down the right edge (behind the dorsal fin and tail, about x 300-400, y 0-260): let the abyss fall away. Lay a radial darkening centred on the lure: clear out to about r 140, then sliding to deep indigo #0A0420 at about .4 opacity by the far corner, above the petals and under the fish. The medallion faces still glow through, just from further down. Why: hyperspace has no floor. Right now the far teal is as bright as the fish's back, so the shadowed side melts into it. With the falloff, the lure's light visibly runs out, and the fish's cyan rim cuts a clean silhouette even at badge size.

The tail fin, right edge (about x 350-392, y 160-245): let the fish dissolve into the fabric. Carry 6 to 8 of the fin rays past the scalloped edge as tapering strokes (from about 0.8 down to 0.2 wide, opacity .6 down to 0) that curl and run into the outlines of the nearest background petals, in the same gold and pink as the rays. Why: in the deep trip, where you end and the pattern begins stops being clear. The loose style wants that edge to bleed, and the far end of the fish is the right place for it, away from the face and the name.

The chin barbel, left of the jaw (the cyan bulb tree, about x 50-105, y 197-238): let the second light *light* something. A soft cyan radial glow (r about 22, opacity .35, screen blend) behind the bulbs, catching the underside of the lower jaw's lip bands and the purple petals just below. Keep it clear of the ribbon's top edge. Why: everything glows in that place, and glow that touches nothing reads as a sticker. Once it spills onto the jaw, the barbel becomes a lamp the fish is carrying.
visions.keep: The SavesFish ribbon with its new neon contour (cream, cyan edge, dark ring, magenta ring, dark ring) on the calm dark band. It reads at once in the 240 px legible.png, so don't let any ring, glow or ray cross it. Also keep the elf mask grinning out of the white-hot lure, the jester elves with their pale almond-eyed faces, the hex tunnel with eyes in its cells falling into the white-gold throat, the glassy crooked fangs with their gold lips, the rune script running through the body bands, the photophore lateral line, and the rainbow nautilus at the pectoral fin. I see the rod got its gold fin-ray rings, but at badge size it still fades into the whirlpool before it reaches the sun. That is yours to judge, artist; I've said my piece on it.

visions.seen: Everything I whispered came true at once: the lure burns tiny in the fish's eye, an elf waits in the white doorway of the throat, and every petal has turned its eye toward the light. But shrink it to a coin and the back half of the fish goes soft, the dorsal fin and tail sinking into the teal medallions like a ghost into wallpaper.
suggestions: The far edge of the fish, from the top of the head (about (180, 55) in the 400 box) over the back, the dorsal fin and the tail, down to where the belly meets the ribbon (about (330, 250)): I see the fish's aura ringing. Stack fat strokes of the fish's silhouette under the fish, widest first: about 20 wide magenta at .25, 15 wide deep indigo at .9, 11 wide violet at .45, 6 wide indigo at .9. That leaves two thin echo rings with dark moats between them hugging the body. Mask them so they are full strength on the far side and fade out toward the lure, leaving the lit face and its white rim light alone, and stop them above the ribbon's top edge. Why: in the breakthrough every outline vibrates outward like a struck bell, and outline, gap, outline is the same banding your neon name already wears. It also cuts the back and tail free of the teal field, so the fish stays a crisp shape at 240 px. That's the crispness you protected when you turned down my bleeding tail, and you were right to.

The glassy fangs on both jaws, the upper row hanging from the slanted upper jaw (about (110, 110) to (215, 175)) and the lower row standing on the gold lower lip (y about 183, x 95 to 220): let the glass split the light. Along the edge of each fang that faces the lure, clip a thin spectral sliver about 1.2 wide (a gradient of red, gold, green, cyan, violet). From the tips of the five or six biggest fangs, throw a tiny fan of three to five rainbow rays, 6 to 10 long at opacity .3, into the dark hex tunnel behind them. Why: in hyperspace white light never stays white. It breaks into spectrum on every crystal edge, and these teeth are the most crystalline thing in the piece. The mouth becomes a jewel box, its tunnel lit by the fish's own teeth.

The dancing elves round the lure (the one on the rod at about (135, 65), the pair below the sun at about (55, 142) and (92, 150)) and the two stragglers drifting in from the dark lower left (about (32, 190) and (35, 235)): give them tracers. Behind each dancer, put two ghost copies of its body, turned back along its orbit round the lure (about (90, 100)) by roughly 8 and 16 degrees, at opacity .28 then .12, tinted cyan then violet. Draw them under the real elf, whose face stays crisp. Give the stragglers longer trails: three or four ghosts shrinking and fading back toward the left edge along a curving path, heading left and up so none reaches the ribbon. Why: tracers are the oldest gift of the trip, a moving thing leaving copies of itself in the air. The stragglers' trails finally show the luring as it happens, the path they drifted in on as the light pulled them out of the dark.
visions.keep: The SavesFish ribbon with its neon contour on the calm dark band. It reads at once in the 240 px test, and no echo ring, ray or tracer should touch it. Keep the gifts you took, too: the tiny esca and bright iris arc on the lure side of the fish's eye, the backlit elf in the throat's doorway, the dim chrysanthemum window in the body, the gem-holding elves, the far eyes turned toward the light, the pulse rings. The rod now reads as one hot magenta hook from forehead to sun even at badge size, so leave it be. Also keep the hex tunnel with eyes in its cells, the rune script in the bands, the rainbow nautilus at the pectoral fin and the barbel's cyan glow on the jaw.
